title: Add graph engine write operations with validation
description: Shared infrastructure: Add createNode, updateNode, deleteNode, createRelation write operations to graph-engine.js with input validation and concurrency protection. Wire write operations to new MCP endpoints in graph.js. Integration test with VectorSearch embedding support.
action: Add write methods (createNode, updateNode, deleteNode, createRelation) to graph-engine.js with input validation. Register write endpoints in graph.js MCP endpoint file. Add frontend API functions in knowledge.ts for graph writes.

criteria: graph-engine.js write methods validate input parameters (type, properties required)
graph.js registers POST endpoints for graph write operations
knowledge.ts exports graph write API functions
Write operations maintain consistency with existing read operations
convergence.verification: Call createNode endpoint, verify node appears in subsequent graphQuery. Delete node, verify removed. Check validation rejects invalid input.
convergence.definition_of_done: Graph engine supports validated CRUD write operations exposed via MCP endpoints and frontend API

files.change: Add createNode(type, properties, id?), updateNode(id, properties), deleteNode(id), createRelation(fromId, toId, type, properties) methods with input validation (required fields, type checking, existence verification).
Add POST /graph/node/create, POST /graph/node/update, POST /graph/node/delete, POST /graph/relation/create endpoints following existing jsonResponse pattern with resolveGraphScope.
Add createGraphNode, updateGraphNode, deleteGraphNode, createGraphRelation async functions calling new MCP endpoints.

implementation: In graph-engine.js: add createNode(type, properties) method — validate type is string, properties is object, generate UUID if no id provided, add to nodes Map, emit change event
In graph-engine.js: add updateNode(id, properties) method — validate node exists, merge properties, update timestamp
In graph-engine.js: add deleteNode(id) method — validate node exists, remove from nodes Map, remove all associated relations
In graph-engine.js: add createRelation(fromId, toId, type, properties) method — validate both nodes exist, validate type string, add to relations Map
In graph.js: register 4 new POST endpoints following existing pattern with resolveGraphScope, parseBody, jsonResponse
In knowledge.ts: add 4 API functions calling new endpoints with proper TypeScript types

integration: Full CRUD cycle: create → query → update → query → delete → verify gone

reference.pattern: Existing graph.js endpoint pattern: resolveGraphScope → graphManager.method → jsonResponse
reference.examples: graph.js lines 10-66 show 3 read-only endpoints with scope resolution pattern

rationale.chosen_approach: Add write operations directly to GraphEngine class, validate at engine level, expose via new endpoints
decision_factors: GraphEngine is the single source of truth for graph data
Desktop app = low contention, simple validation sufficient
rationale.tradeoffs: Adding to GraphEngine increases class size, but write ops are natural extensions of read architecture

risks.mitigation: Input validation at engine level, existence checks before mutations, node deletion cascades to relations

risks.risk: VectorSearch embedding not triggered on write
risks.mitigation: Reuse existing setVectorSearch() DI pattern, trigger embedding in createNode/createRelation

affected_requirements: Shared infrastructure for F2 and F6
